alternative: Model the node set as an enum and write each operation as a function that matches on it: dispatch is exhaustive, compiler-checked and free of vtables. If the node set genuinely has to stay open across crate or plugin boundaries, use a trait-object protocol with an explicit Any/TypeId registry or custom downcast boundary, accepting that a failed lookup is a runtime miss rather than a compiler error.
idiom_name: enum + match (recommended); Any downcast only at open plugin boundaries
implementation_notes: Rust has no class inheritance, multiple inheritance or cross-cast, so Martin's C++ acyclic visitor has no direct idiomatic encoding. For a closed AST, enum plus match is the right replacement: each operation matches every variant and the compiler checks coverage. At an open plugin boundary, a trait object can expose Any and callers can downcast to a concrete plugin operation or use a TypeId-keyed registry, but that is an explicit runtime protocol - not a per-element visitor interface - and a failed lookup must be handled. Keep this discouraged form only when openness across crate boundaries outweighs static exhaustiveness; otherwise choose enum and match.
pitfalls: Trying to reproduce the cross-cast with Any::downcast_mut::<AreaVisitor> matches only that exact concrete visitor type, so another visitor implementing the same operation is skipped; use enum/match for a closed set or document a concrete plugin registry for an open boundary.

Putting a borrowed visitor behind Any fails because Any is 'static and types containing non-'static references do not implement it; keep a borrowed trait-object protocol or move owned state into the visitor instead.

Adding a wildcard arm to make enum match compile hides future variants from the compiler, so a new node reaches a runtime default instead of a required implementation; omit the wildcard when exhaustive coverage is the goal.
